statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band while the overnight recovery proceeds with retracements intact, against an elevated-stress macro backdrop.
recommendation: Tail stays below the watch threshold on current evidence. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the 13:30Z US cash open through 15:30Z, spanning the opening auction and the 14:00Z University of Michigan preliminary sentiment and inflation-expectations release.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures recover most of the AI-led decline; Tail low, Stress elevated on energy and long-end yields
body: Nasdaq-100 cash closed 8 October at 30,725.81, down 1.39%, after a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue is roughly $20bn below previously indicated levels. The decline was concentrated rather than broad: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.4% and Oracle lost more than 5%, while the Dow rose 0.1% and the Russell 2000 finished flat. Overnight, NQ futures based at 30,953 and advanced to 31,220.75, near the session high of 31,228.75, recovering most of the cash decline, and Asia-Pacific cash markets closed mostly higher. VIX near 15.3 is below its 15.41 prior close. That combination describes mean reversion functioning rather than failing, so Tail stays in the low band. Stress remains elevated for reasons independent of today's path: Brent near 103.3 after a 4.1% session gain and WTI near 90.9 on Iran-linked supply risk, 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields near 24-year highs at roughly 5.28% and 5.67%, and University of Michigan sentiment close to 48. Breadth that diverged from the Nasdaq decline reduces directional conviction rather than confirming a one-way path. The scheduled checkpoints are the 13:30Z cash open, the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release with 1-year inflation expectations near 4.6%, and a Fed Collins appearance at 20:00Z. CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00Z, so the final ten slots of the forecast cover a period with no NQ price discovery, where in-hour path risk is structurally low and evidence freshness decays.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours began with a watch-band European and US session on 8 October, peaking at Tail 28 and Stress 72 at 17:00Z as the AI-revenue report drove the Nasdaq-100 to a 1.39% decline and the semiconductor index to -3.4%. Risk then eased steadily through the overnight hours as futures recovered and volatility contracted, with Tail back in the low band from 20:00Z onward and Stress declining from 72 to 54.
outlookSummary: The low-Tail reading holds through the European session while the overnight recovery retains retracements. Tail rises into a watch band across the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release, peaking at 23 in the 14:00Z slot, then decays if price discovery stays orderly. A second watch-band slot covers the 20:00Z Friday close and the scheduled Fed Collins appearance. From 21:00Z the CME equity index futures halt removes NQ price discovery for the remaining ten slots, where in-hour Tail sits at a structural floor and Confidence decays with distance from verified live evidence.
